native_memory.storage_method: Static LLVM inspection only. Check real header/capture bytes, alignment and nonoverlap; ARC excludes tracing symbols and the tracing control retains them. Initial zero capture words are filled during startup; Linux startup instructions are checked separately. No binary execution.

native_memory.scope: Current fwp tracing and checked ARC servers handle identical sequential HTTP/2 GET /hello requests from an ordinary native ARC client over loopback. Each body is received and released; status 200 is summed. Inputs 1, 16 and 256 calls, cleartext and TLS, three fresh measured server processes per case; an ordinary server is the output control. Every server then handles one HTTP/1.1 /stop request, drains children and exits. Managed counters begin after constant initialization and end after entry execution and cached-value cleanup, before complete runtime shutdown; they include server startup, the requested calls and the fixed shutdown request. Collection is disabled and freeing enabled in both modes. Counters exclude raw transport/TLS buffers, allocator metadata/pages and client memory. Separately, ordinary uninstrumented servers receive five batches of 4096 calls each; each batch starts a fresh client process, and the server's 1000-request connection limit exercises connection replacement within each batch. Current server resident memory is sampled after each client exits and a 100 ms settling interval; the first batch warms caches and the next four must remain within 8 MiB of that first sample. Linux uses /proc VmRSS, macOS ps RSS and Windows process WorkingSet64; these are resident-memory samples, not allocated/live-value counts. Native -O2 with normal compiler optimization and -ffp-contract=off. This compares memory modes at one revision; it makes no speed or C/Rust parity claim. Source, generated C, ordinary/instrumented binaries, raw counter rows, RSS samples and stderr are retained. Separate counters record entries into the generic ownership check through cached-value cleanup. Instrumentation can prevent check elimination/inlining, so these are instrumented executions, not ordinary machine-call counts. The counted client runs against a control server; its work is excluded from measured-server allocation rows.
